chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Is'haq ibn Abi Al-Hilal, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

Amir Al-Momineen (peace be upon him) said: 'Shall I inform you of the great adultery?' They said, 'Yes.' He said: 'It is a woman who tramples the bed of her husband, then brings a child from someone else, and imposes him upon her husband. So that is the one whom Allah will not speak to, nor will He look at her on the Day of Resurrection, nor will He purify her, and for her is a painful punishment.'

key_terms.تُوطِئُ فِرَاشَ زَوْجِهَا: She tramples/occupies the bed of her husband
key_terms.لَا يَنْظُرُ إِلَيْهَا: He will not look at her
key_terms.لَا يُكَلِّمُهَا اللَّهُ: Allah will not speak to her

ai.seo_question: What is considered the 'great adultery' in Shia tradition involving false paternity?
ai.summary: In this narration from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) attributes to Imam Ali (AS) the identification of 'major adultery' not merely as sexual intercourse, but specifically as the deception of paternity (al-kiswah) where a woman bears a child by another man and claims him as her husband's. This form is considered grave because it alters lineage and inheritance rights, leading to divine rejection characterized by Allah not speaking to her, not looking at her with mercy, and facing a painful punishment. This highlights the Shia emphasis on the integrity of lineage (nasab) as a core component of marital fidelity.
